body:
From the logs in the report and the source on `main` (665fc18), the re-prefill looks like the RAM-hit/disk-lookup gap tracked in #411 (open fix: #436), not a retention refusal:

- The serve path consults the disk tier only after a RAM miss: `src/cli/serve/text_model_runner.cpp:1877` checks `!lease.cache_hit()` before `RestoreLongestPrefix`. The 4,068-token RAM entry is a hit, so the 168,973-token disk entry is never looked up. Each turn logs `cache=memory cached_tokens=4068`. That check is the same in v0.10.0.
- The `byte_capacity` skips are expected no matter what the eviction policy does. Each deep checkpoint is larger than the whole RAM budget: `bytes=4730881496` and `bytes=4759381792` against `capacity_bytes=4593364992`. Evicting older entries would not let it fit. So expected behavior 1 cannot help with this budget; behavior 2 (deepest match across RAM and disk) is what #436 implements.

#503 and #517 add the component cache under `src/cache/`. At v0.11.0, no file under `src/cli/` or `src/models/` includes `src/cache/`, so I don't think they are on this serving path.

Why 0.10.0 had no short RAM hit here is my unverified hypothesis. Between v0.10.0 and v0.11.0, the only change under `src/cli/serve/continuation_cache.cpp` is #476. It promotes a restored checkpoint to a branch point when a later prompt diverges from a deeper peer (`RestoreDiverges`). `TestRestoredSharedPrefixOutlivesFrozenFrontiers` shows that such a branch point is retained ahead of older turns. A shared ~4k system-prompt checkpoint would therefore now stay resident in RAM and hide the deeper disk entry, where 0.10.0 could evict it and fall through to disk. I have not reproduced this with the reporter's workload.

> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.

Test scope: source reading plus one unit-test run. I compared v0.10.0, v0.11.0 and `main` with `git diff`/`grep` and built and ran `continuation_cache_test` (passed) on a CPU host with the `cpu-test` preset. No model was loaded, the reporter's workload was not reproduced, and #436 was not tested against this case.
